title: 11-day education equality campaign starts in Balaghat

quick: An 11-day campaign for equal access to quality education began in Balaghat, Madhya Pradesh on November 15. Organized by a committee, the yatra will travel to Bhopal by November 25, passing through Seoni, Chhindwara, Betul, and Narmadapuram districts.

body: An 11-day campaign advocating equal access to quality education began in Balaghat district of Madhya Pradesh on November 15. The initiative, organized by a committee, is structured as a yatra that will conclude in Bhopal on November 25.

The yatra will pass through four districts along its route: Seoni, Chhindwara, Betul, and Narmadapuram. The committee stated the journey aims to highlight the need for equitable educational opportunities across the region.

body: CBSE has announced its Expression Series for the 2026-27 academic year, inviting students from Classes III to XII to participate in activities centered on women empowerment and gender equality.

title: NEET 2026: Float and Freeze option leaves medical seats vacant
description: New admission flexibility lets candidates hold seats without joining, contributing to hundreds of unfilled medical seats despite high exam turnout.
quick: The 2026 NEET counselling introduced a Float and Freeze option allowing candidates to carry forward seat allotments without completing admission formalities. Even if seats remain unchanged in Round 3, candidates can decline to join. This flexibility has led to significant seat underutilisation, with hundreds of medical seats…
points: Float and Freeze option introduced in 2026 NEET counselling
Candidates can hold allotments without completing admission
Seats can be declined even after Round 3 allotment
Flexibility linked to hundreds of vacant medical seats
Millions of students appeared for NEET 2026
body: The 2026 NEET counselling process included a Float and Freeze option that permits candidates to retain their seat allotments without finishing admission procedures. This provision applies even if the allotted seat does not change in the third round of counselling.

Because candidates can choose not to join after holding a seat, many allotted positions remain unfilled. The Hindu reports that this flexibility has had significant implications for seat utilisation, resulting in hundreds of medical seats going vacant despite the large number of test-takers.

faq.q: What is the Float and Freeze option in NEET 2026?
faq.a: It allows candidates to carry forward their seat allotments without completing admission formalities and decline the seat even if it remains unchanged in Round 3.

faq.q: How has this option affected medical seat availability?
faq.a: The flexibility has led to significant seat underutilisation, with hundreds of medical seats remaining vacant despite millions of students taking NEET.

source.name: The Hindu
source.title: Millions of students take NEET, yet hundreds of medical seats go vacant

title: RBI to auction 91-day, 182-day and 364-day Treasury Bills on Nov 18
description: The Reserve Bank of India will auction three Treasury Bills worth a total of ₹23,000 crore on November 18, 2026, with settlement on November 19.
quick: The Reserve Bank of India has announced an auction of three Government of India Treasury Bills on November 18, 2026, totalling ₹23,000 crore. The 91-day and 182-day bills are notified at ₹8,000 crore each, and the 364-day bill at ₹7,000 crore. Settlement is on November 19, 2026.
points: The 91-day and 182-day bills are notified at ₹8,000 crore each.
The 364-day bill is notified at ₹7,000 crore, taking the total to ₹23,000 crore.
Bids will be submitted electronically on the RBI's E-Kuber system on November 18.
Retail investors can bid non-competitively, capped at 5 percent of the notified amount.
Successful bidders must pay on November 19, 2026.
body: The Reserve Bank of India will auction three Treasury Bills of the Government of India on Wednesday, November 18, 2026. The 91-day and 182-day bills carry a notified amount of ₹8,000 crore each, while the 364-day bill is notified at ₹7,000 crore, adding up to ₹23,000 crore.

The auction will be price based and use the multiple price method. Competitive bids can be placed between 10:30 am and 11:30 am, and non-competitive bids between 10:30 am and 11:00 am, in electronic form on the RBI's E-Kuber system. Results are to be announced on the auction day, and payment by successful bidders is due on Thursday, November 19, 2026.

State governments, Union Territories with a legislature, eligible provident funds in India, designated foreign central banks and other specified institutions may take part on a non-competitive basis, with that allocation falling outside the notified amount. Individuals can also participate as retail investors through the Retail Direct portal, limited to a maximum of 5 percent of the notified amount.

The sale is subject to the terms of the General Notification F.No.4(2)-B(W&M)/2018 dated March 26, 2025, as amended from time to time. Physical bids will be accepted only if the system fails, and must reach the Public Debt Office before the auction timing ends.

faq.q: When is the RBI Treasury Bill auction in November 2026?
faq.a: The auction is on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, with settlement on Thursday, November 19, 2026.
A total of ₹23,000 crore: ₹8,000 crore in 91-day bills, ₹8,000 crore in 182-day bills and ₹7,000 crore in 364-day bills.
Yes, individuals can bid on a non-competitive basis through the Retail Direct portal, with allocation restricted to a maximum of 5 percent of the notified amount.
